selected_compute_spec.note: Confirmed x86_64 (non-aarch64/non-Graviton) after this session's fix to resolve_lts_spark_version/resolve_node_type. This spec was NOT the cause of the failure below -- the same class of error occurred with a corrected, architecturally-compatible spec.

cluster_create_attempt.exception: TimeoutError: Timed out after 0:05:00 | caused by BadRequest: Current organization <REDACTED_ORG_ID> does not have any associated worker environments
cluster_create_attempt.root_cause: The POST /api/2.1/clusters/create request itself was rejected by the Databricks backend with a BadRequest whose message ('does not have any associated worker environments') is one of the specific substrings databricks-sdk's own BaseClient._is_retryable() treats as transient. The SDK's HTTP client (databricks.sdk._base_client.BaseClient, default retry_timeout_seconds=300) silently retried this request for the full 5 minutes before giving up and raising TimeoutError -- so no cluster object was ever created on the backend at any point, and this specific 5-minute figure came entirely from the SDK's own transport-layer retry default, not from this project's own cluster_timeout_seconds polling config (which never had a chance to run, since create() itself never returned a cluster_id).
cluster_create_attempt.interpretation: This is a genuine workspace/organization-level limitation, not a permission/entitlement problem (the identity has the allow-cluster-create entitlement) and not the earlier aarch64/x86_64 architecture-mismatch bug (already fixed and confirmed not to be the cause here, since the corrected spec still failed identically). This specific Databricks organization does not have a 'worker environment' provisioned for classic cluster compute.

final_cluster_state: N/A -- no cluster_id was ever obtained; the cluster never reached PENDING
cleanup_result: Nothing to clean up. Confirmed via `databricks clusters list` (against the same profile) returning zero clusters both before and after this attempt.
recommended_compute_mode_correction: An earlier version of this evidence file recommended job_cluster. That was corrected: a Jobs new_cluster is STILL classic jobs compute under the hood (it goes through the same cluster-manager/worker-environment infrastructure as a standalone cluster, just job-scoped) and would be expected to fail identically to the explicit_cluster attempt above, for the same organization-level reason. It is therefore not a meaningfully different infrastructure path and is not the preferred next thing to try in this workspace.
recommended_compute_mode_rationale: Explicit classic cluster creation (compute_mode=explicit_cluster) is proven unavailable in this specific workspace/organization due to the missing 'worker environment' backend condition above -- this is unrelated to and unaffected by ClusterSpec correctness. serverless_job (a job task with no existing_cluster_id, new_cluster, or job_cluster_key at all, so Databricks selects serverless compute) is the genuinely distinct, Databricks-managed compute path that does not depend on this organization's classic-compute worker-environment infrastructure. Because the classic-compute failure surfaces as TimeoutError (via the SDK's own retry-and-give-up behavior), not as PermissionDenied/InvalidParameterValue, LAB 09's automatic exception-driven fallback (compute.try_start_cluster_create) does not and should not self-select serverless_job or job_cluster from a bare timeout -- per this task's explicit instruction not to broadly catch TimeoutError and treat it as a permission-style rejection, since an ordinary timeout could just as easily mean something else entirely. Instead, this workspace's choice is recorded deliberately in config/dev.yml's compute.preferred_mode, which `run-all --compute-mode auto` reads directly rather than rediscovering the same failure on every run. (Serverless execution has since been confirmed live in separate, later, targeted validations -- see evidence/LIVE_VALIDATION_SUMMARY.md.)
